issue: BT-0051 is a duplicate of BT-0050: the same Reece Plumbing Supply bill (invoice 88412, $1,848.00) entered twice, and only BT-0050 is on the bank statement.
proposed_fix: Delete or void BT-0051 ($1,848.00, Reference "88412"). Keep BT-0050, which is reconciled to SL-0050. This removes $1,680.00 of overstated Materials (310) and the $168.00 GST credit claimed twice.
evidence: BT-0050: Contact Reece Plumbing Supply, Date 2026-08-11, Reference "INV 88412", Total 1848.00 (LineAmount 1680.00, TaxAmount 168.00, 310/INPUT), IsReconciled true, matched by SL-0050 (2026-08-11, REECE PLUMBING SUPPLY, -1848.00). BT-0051: Contact Reece Plumbing Supply, Date 2026-08-12, Reference "88412", Total 1848.00 (LineAmount 1680.00, TaxAmount 168.00, 310/INPUT), IsReconciled false, and no statement line is matched to BT-0051.

issue: A laptop costing $2,635.45 ex GST is over the $1,000 capitalise threshold and lasts more than a year, but it was expensed to Repairs and Maintenance.
proposed_fix: Recode the $2,635.45 line from 473 Repairs and Maintenance to 720 Computer Equipment (fixed asset) and add it to the fixed asset register for depreciation. The GST of $263.55 is unchanged and belongs to the GST reviewer.
evidence: BT-0046, 2026-08-16, Contact JB Hi-Fi Business (default account 720), Description "Laptop for estimator", AccountCode 473, TaxType INPUT, LineAmount 2635.45, TaxAmount 263.55, Total 2899.00. Organisation Policies.CapitaliseThreshold 1000.0.

issue: A joinery install by a subcontractor on job J-118 was coded to Materials instead of Subcontractors, which misstates job costing.
proposed_fix: Recode the $5,800.00 line from 310 Materials to 315 Subcontractors. If the Pinewood invoice includes supplied materials as a separate line, split it: materials to 310 and labour or install to 315. Confirm this against the invoice.
evidence: BT-0047, 2026-08-22, Contact Pinewood Joinery (default account 315; other Pinewood claims BT-0030, BT-0031 and BT-0033 are coded 315), Description "Joinery install, job J-118", AccountCode 310, TaxType INPUT, LineAmount 5800.00, TaxAmount 580.00, Total 6380.00.

issue: Statement line SL-0051 ($1,524.00 paid to Coastal Electrical) is matched to BT-0052, but BT-0052 totals $1,254.00, so the two differ by $270.00; this looks like a transposition error when BT-0052 was keyed into Xero.
proposed_fix: The bank amount is the actual cash that left the account, so the Xero side is most likely wrong. Check Coastal Electrical Contractors' progress claim for job J-124. If the claim is $1,524.00 incl GST, amend BT-0052 to Total 1524.00 (LineAmount 1385.45, GST 138.55) and re-reconcile it. If the claim really is $1,254.00, the payment was $270.00 too much: ask the supplier for a refund or credit and record the $270.00 difference. Unmatch SL-0051 until one of these is done.
evidence: SL-0051: Date 2026-08-24, Payee "COASTAL ELECTRICAL CON", Amount -1524.00, MatchedTransactionID BT-0052. BT-0052: Contact Coastal Electrical Contractors, Date 2026-08-24, Description "Progress claim, job J-124", 315/INPUT, LineAmount 1140.00, TaxAmount 114.00, Total 1254.00, IsReconciled true. Difference 270.00, which divides by 9, the usual sign of transposed digits (1524 vs 1254).

issue: Groceries from Woolworths were paid from the company account and coded to Entertainment, and they look like private spending.
proposed_fix: Ask the client whether this was a business expense, for example staff amenities or a client function. If not, recode the full $214.35 to 880 Owner A Drawings as BAS Excluded, with no GST credit. This reverses the $19.49 credit.
evidence: BT-0048, 2026-08-23, Contact Woolworths, Description "Groceries", AccountCode 420 Entertainment, TaxType INPUT, LineAmount 194.86, TaxAmount 19.49, Total 214.35.

issue: GST was calculated as 10% of the GST-inclusive total instead of total divided by 11, so the GST credit is overstated by $19.80.
proposed_fix: Change TaxAmount from 217.80 to 198.00 and LineAmount from 1,960.20 to 1,980.00. Total stays 2,178.00. This reduces the GST credit by $19.80.
evidence: BT-0045, 2026-08-09, Laminex Direct (C003, IsGSTRegistered true), "Benchtop laminate, job J-124", AccountCode 310, TaxType INPUT, LineAmount 1960.20, TaxAmount 217.80, Total 2178.00. 2178.00 / 11 = 198.00; 217.80 = 10% of 2178.00.

issue: Statement line SL-0052, an $8,420.00 payment to the ATO, has no matching Xero transaction, so it is missing from the books.
proposed_fix: This is most likely the BAS/IAS payment for GST and PAYG withholding (for July or the prior quarter). Ask the client for the ATO statement of account or the lodged BAS/IAS showing $8,420.00 due. Then record an $8,420.00 spend money transaction to the ATO, coded BAS Excluded against GST liability / PAYG Withholding Payable (or the ATO clearing account) and split per that statement, and reconcile it to SL-0052. Do not post anything until the client confirms what the payment covers.
evidence: SL-0052: Date 2026-08-28, Payee "ATO PAYMENT", Amount -8420.00, MatchedTransactionID null. None of the 52 Xero bank transactions (BT-0001 to BT-0052) has an ATO contact or a total of 8420.00.

issue: A 12-month contract works insurance policy running to 31 Jul 2027 was expensed in full in August instead of going to Prepayments.
proposed_fix: Recode the $4,800.00 ex-GST amount from 433 Insurance to 620 Prepayments, then release $400.00 a month ($4,800.00 / 12) to 433 Insurance, starting August 2026. At 31 Aug 2026 that leaves $400.00 in 433 and $4,400.00 in 620. The $480.00 GST credit stays claimed in August.
evidence: BT-0049, 2026-08-02, Contact QBE Insurance, Description "Contract works insurance, 12 months to 31 Jul 2027", AccountCode 433, TaxType INPUT, LineAmount 4800.00, TaxAmount 480.00, Total 5280.00. Organisation Policies.CapitaliseThreshold 1000.0.

issue: A GST credit of $360.00 was claimed on a payment to a supplier who is not registered for GST.
proposed_fix: Change TaxType from INPUT to GST free (no GST credit) and set TaxAmount to 0.00 and LineAmount to 3,960.00. Total stays 3,960.00. This reverses the $360.00 credit. Ask the client whether Ridge Tiling's invoice actually showed GST. If it did, the supplier should not have charged GST, and the client should ask for a corrected invoice or a refund.
evidence: BT-0043, 2026-08-26, Ridge Tiling (sole trader) (C006, TaxNumber 71 824 330 016, IsGSTRegistered false), "Tiling, job J-121", AccountCode 315, TaxType INPUT, LineAmount 3600.00, TaxAmount 360.00, Total 3960.00.

issue: A casual wages payment is coded INPUT with a $300.00 GST credit, but wages are BAS Excluded and carry no GST.
proposed_fix: Change TaxType from INPUT to BASEXCLUDED and set TaxAmount to 0.00 and LineAmount to 3,300.00 in account 477. Total stays 3,300.00. This reverses the $300.00 credit.
evidence: BT-0044, 2026-08-17, Payroll Clearing (C020, IsGSTRegistered false), "Weekly wages (casual)", AccountCode 477 (Wages and Salaries, default TaxType BASEXCLUDED), TaxType INPUT, LineAmount 3000.00, TaxAmount 300.00, Total 3300.00. The other wage runs (BT-0001 to BT-0005) are BASEXCLUDED with TaxAmount 0.00.

issue: A bank fee is coded INPUT with a $5.90 GST credit, but under the firm's rules bank fees are input taxed and get no GST credit.
proposed_fix: Change TaxType from INPUT to EXEMPTEXPENSES (input taxed) and set TaxAmount to 0.00 and LineAmount to 64.90 in account 404. Total stays 64.90. This reverses the $5.90 credit.
evidence: BT-0042, 2026-08-31, Commonwealth Bank (C019), "Merchant facility fee", AccountCode 404 (Bank Fees, default TaxType EXEMPTEXPENSES), TaxType INPUT, LineAmount 59.00, TaxAmount 5.90, Total 64.90. The account keeping fee BT-0041 on the same account is EXEMPTEXPENSES with TaxAmount 0.00.
